messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: service/redwood-runtime - 95p latency breaching SLA (current: 1.28s, SLO: 700ms) and 5xx rate increased to 2.3% (threshold 0.5%). Paging primary on-call.

alex.chen: on it. I see the spike corresponds with the cache eviction rollout started ~15m ago. Mira — are you still running that deploy? :eyes:

mira.patel: yes, rollout is in progress. We throttled to 10% but looks like some backend workers are saturating. I'm pausing the rollout now.

samir.khan: tagging for visibility — customers on Dedicated clusters possibly impacted. Recommending we temporarily relax the p95 alert to reduce noise while mitigation finishes.

elena: +1. We should communicate any threshold change and duration. Customer-facing SLAs unchanged; this is for paging noise suppression only.

alex.chen: proposed change: raise p95 latency alert from 700ms -> 1.2s for the next 90 minutes and increase 5xx alert threshold from 0.5% -> 2.5% until rollout paused and caches warm. Will add a runbook pointer to revert. Any objections?

mira.patel: fine by me, helps avoid paging for noisy but transient rollout effects.

samir.khan: quick customer impact note: internal logs show ~120 requests/min experiencing >1s latency; estimated affected DTUs: small fraction of traffic but a few dedicated customers seeing degraded completion times. No errors for core auth or metadata. I'll open a post-incident customer note draft after mitigation.

alex.chen: executing threshold change now. command:```
opsctl alert update --service redwood-runtime --rule p95-latency --threshold 1200 --until "+90m" --comment "oncall: temporary threshold increase during cache eviction rollout (pause in progress). revert scheduled"
opsctl alert update --service redwood-runtime --rule error-rate-5xx --threshold 2.5 --until "+90m" --comment "oncall: temporary"
```

ops-bot: opsctl: Alerts updated successfully:
- p95-latency -> 1200ms (expires in 90m)
- error-rate-5xx -> 2.5% (expires in 90m)

alex.chen: perf dashboards look calmer after pausing rollout and the temporary threshold change — 95p down to ~1.05s now, 5xx trending down.

mira.patel: I'll resume a slower rollout only after we validate cache warmup. Plan: 1% increments, 5m hold, health checks on worker cpu/queue depth. Runbook here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-eviction (see section "safe-rollout")

samir.khan: I'm drafting the customer impact note: short summary + timeframe + mitigation + rollback plan. Will link to the incident postmortem once we close.

elena: coverage gap: next oncall shift (UTC+2) doesn't overlap with Mira by more than 10m. Alex, can you add a quick handoff message with the exact timestamps and who to page for infra?

alex.chen: sure. Handoff plan: I'm primary until 1713012000 (approx in 2h). Samir will be secondary. After 1713012000 Mira will be primary until 1713026400 (she's the deploy owner). If anything escalates with Dedicated customers page @samir.khan directly. Please check the alert expiry — opsctl set expiry for 90m, scheduled revert at 171301+; I'll set a follow-up revert task.

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: revert-alerts (runs at 1713012205)

samir.khan: noted. I'll monitor Dedicated customer queues and begin the customer note in #customer-success.

alex.chen: quick checklist for whoever picks up: 1) confirm opsctl expiry is set, 2) validate caches warming (key hit rate > 80%), 3) confirm p95 < 900ms for 5 continuous minutes, 4) revert alerts and close the loop with customers. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/incident-paging (section "adjusting-alert-thresholds").

mira.patel: thanks — re: revert, I'll only continue rollout after we meet the health criteria. If we fail to meet them within 90m we escalate to infra for scaling.

alex.chen: ok handoff complete. primary: alex.chen until 1713012000; secondary: samir.khan. open actions: samir -> customer note, mira -> controlled rollout checks, alex -> ensure alert revert. :white_check_mark:

samir.khan: I'll post the customer note draft in ~30m. If anyone wants to add specifics please ping me.

incident-bot: NOTE: This thread will be archived when alerts return to normal and the oncall marks the incident resolved.
